sections.title: Employment Contract
sections.text:
S.E.E.S. member Yukari Takeba, cheerful in temperament and radiant in appearance.

Her way with people is plain for all to see—yet there is a side of her that is hard to approach.

sections.text: A phone-strap doll, a little worn, but plainly kept with care all this time. If you have something you want to say, it will surely listen.

sections.title: Student Overview
sections.text:
Yukari Takeba. Registered in March of 1102 at the Atrium Notary Office as a Category III resident; admitted to Saint Marcel Comprehensive School pursuant to Article 36 of the appendix to the Charter of Lateran Citizens' Rights and Chapter 2, Article 5 of the Regulations on the Administration of Entrants.
Teacher's remarks: Yukari Takeba is bright and kind, gentle and cheerful, skilled at communication, and possessed of a strong sense of independence. In the firearm-like armament course series, her archery left a deep impression on the instructors. It is hoped that when she meets difficulties she will not hesitate to accept help from her teachers and classmates, and will join everyone in building a warm, harmonious class where all support one another.

sections.title: Archive File 1
sections.text:
Yukari settled into school life in Laterano in no time. On her first day she exchanged contacts with the class president; on the third, she learned the shortcut from the dormitory to the school building from Stitch in the tenth grade; by the fifth, the woman at the school shop already knew her name. Then, through joint practice with the archery club, Yukari even acquired several friends she was on speaking terms with in other classes and years.
She also became the point of contact drawing the other students and the transfer students' little group together—picking up the thread naturally when Makoto fell silent, and smoothing over the awkwardness when Aigis asked one of her strange questions. Amiya wondered about it: why did Yukari adapt to a new environment so quickly? Yukari shrugged. "Ah... probably because I've had practice? It's not the first time." For some reason her smile carried a trace of self-mockery. Perhaps she caught the faint worry in Amiya's eyes, because she quickly recovered her usual brightness. "It's fine. That experience came in handy, didn't it? Don't worry about it."

sections.title: Archive File 2
sections.text:
Because she enrolled late, Yukari was not able to try the profession that interested her during the volunteer placement. Yukari herself did not mind, but Amiya, who had already become her friend, kept feeling a little sorry about it. That regret was made up for by chance.
One day, on their way to the supermarket with Amiya, Yukari was stopped by a Liberi friar with a bow and quiver on his back. He asked the two of them to model for some photographs to be used in a magazine advertisement. "To break into the school shop's supply chain, we must raise the profile of our monastery's bread among the students...!" said the friar. Amiya seemed to know the monastery he came from, and at her urging Yukari took the job with her.
Later, two great baskets of monastery bread arrived at the dorm as payment, and only then did her companions learn what had happened. "The friar looked so pitiful begging like that... and it's only photos, s-so what's the harm! All right, all right, enough about that—hurry up and eat the bread!" The photo on the dorm's picture wall of a red-faced Yukari brandishing a loaf is said to date from exactly this moment.

sections.title: Archive File 3
sections.text:
After the volunteer work, the transfer students became friends with the two attendants they had met at the Requiem Funeral Hall, and Yukari was no exception. Hearing that Giada also does volunteer service at the Requiem Chapel outside the mobile city in her time off, Yukari went along with her on one of her days off.
Resting in the flower field outside the Requiem Chapel, Yukari asked Giada, "I remember something you mentioned once... that in the past there were no Liberi funeral directors in Laterano. Is that one of Laterano's rules too?"
"There is no such rule."
"Is that some kind of social perception...?"
"'Social perception'... perhaps. Liberi can't share in empathy, after all, so in the past we were indeed thought unable to hold command of an occasion like a funeral."
"So even studying as hard as you did wasn't enough...? Maybe it's because I don't understand Laterano, but 'you can't do it because you're Liberi'—somehow I really don't like that." Yukari's expression grew complicated.
Giada gave a helpless laugh. "It's probably not as bad as you make it sound, Yukari... Although I have wondered—if that hadn't happened with the Law, I'd never have had the chance to become a funeral director now... Maybe it's wrong of me to think that way."
"...I don't think that's it." Yukari shook her head earnestly. "Maybe the change in the Law gave you an opening, but isn't it because you've always taken the work of a funeral director seriously and kept at it, Giada, that you were able to make it happen?"
She went on: "Liberi are Lateran too, aren't they? When circumstances change, different people can bring out different strengths... and that change is something you achieved yourself, Giada. That's how I see it, at least..." Then she suddenly waved her hands in a fluster. "Ah—why am I suddenly talking so seriously..."
A rare, gentle smile appeared on Giada's face. "No. You're quite right. I'll remember that."

sections.title: Archive File 4
sections.text:
There was once a question Yukari tried to ask me.
The infirmary had already closed for the day, so I took Yukari, who had just finished training, to the hospital where a doctor I know works, to pick up some analgesic spray.
When we reached the consulting room, my doctor friend was still seeing the last returning patient. The patient's daughter was waiting outside; the Executor who usually stays at her side did not seem to be around, so we sat with the child for a while. On learning that Yukari was "a transfer student from the East," Cecilia asked a whole string of curious questions, and Yukari answered them deftly—without giving away her "unknown origins," yet satisfying the child's curiosity all the same. Children are often far more perceptive than adults; from a moment's hesitation or one strained word they can tell whether the person they are talking to is sincere, or is brushing them off. It is the wariness of those in a weaker position. Yukari knows that wariness—it springs from the same root as her own self-protection, and it lets her form a gentle understanding with children like Cecilia. In less than ten minutes of conversation, Cecilia had come to like this "foreign big sister." But when Cecilia turned the subject to her own mother, Yukari fell into an unnatural silence. Worse, Cecilia noticed it, and the second half of the question—"Where do you and your mom go when you go out together, Yukari?"—dissolved into a mumble. Fortunately Felia stepped out of the consulting room just then, and Yukari took the chance to change the subject.
After accepting with a smile Cecilia's invitation to "go get sweets together next time," Yukari watched the mother and daughter leave the hospital hand in hand. Her mood had clearly sunk.
"Doctor..." Her voice, as she asked, was as small as if she were speaking to herself. "If a child were to feel, toward her mother..."
She did not finish the sentence, and I acted as though I had not heard, merely reminding her that we ought to go in and get the analgesic spray from Dr. Kal'tsit.
I do not think she needs to seek the answer to that question from anyone else. What is the right answer for one person is not necessarily right for another. Anyone may fail to love someone, and the reverse is equally true. I believe that one day Yukari will find the answer she hopes for.

sections.title: Encrypted Report
sections.text:
Yukari Takeba, like the other members of S.E.E.S., has the ability to summon a "Persona." But unlike Makoto Yuki or Aigis, there are not so many mysteries about her. She is essentially much closer to an ordinary secondary school student, and for a time my investigation stalled for want of anything to aim at. Still, piecing together information from several channels, I did eventually reach some conclusions.
Yukari joined S.E.E.S. to find the truth about her father's death. While investigating a certain accident from years ago, circumstances led her into the group. She has her reason to fight, and troubles buried deep inside, and she can only face and untangle all of it herself. What can be confirmed, though, is that the truth she is chasing has nothing to do with your concerns or mine. In sum, she has strong motive to return to her original world, and once S.E.E.S. locates the gate, Yukari will go back along with the rest.
...I hope she learns the truth she is seeking, and that the truth does not disappoint her. I do not know what her father went through, but the deeds of one generation dragging the next into the whirl of fate—that is common enough anywhere. No elder would welcome it, and yet none can stop it either... Even if ours is only a passing acquaintance, old friend, join me in wishing these children well.
